title: Send unmet acceptance criteria back to the producer before verifying
summary: Extend the producer report with a per-criterion self-check against the accepted reading's acceptance criteria. In the producer loop in run.rs, any unmet or missing criterion goes back to the producer once, in the same working directory, before the candidate reaches the verifier. A lifecycle test shows an unmet criterion is reported to the producer and fixed before verification. The audience is the Athena maintainer, who judges whether the verifier stops being the first to find unmet criteria.

defaults_applied.how: The change and the tests are Rust.
The change adds lifecycle tests, and cargo test and clippy must pass.
The rule is enforced in the producer loop, not only stated in the prompt.
It generalizes the existing send-back path, not a single case.
One focused change that reuses the existing loop.
Behavior is checked by running the new tests.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The check is self-reported: the producer's report gains a criteria_check list, one entry per accepted criterion (criterion text, status met/unmet, evidence). Athena checks the list is complete and has no unmet entries, and it does not judge whether the evidence is true.

It reuses the existing send-back loop in produce_and_verify (PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS) and does not add a new stage. An unmet or missing criterion after the allowed send-backs fails the job before verification, the same as a missing full test run.
Every unmet criterion is listed in the send-back brief in one message.
A criterion is matched by its exact text from the accepted reading; a missing entry counts as unmet.

Pinned studies, which have no tests, keep their exemption from the test send-back; the criteria check applies to them only if they have acceptance criteria, and the same rule applies to both capabilities.
The send-back budget is shared: one send-back round covers both the test and the criteria problems, and both are reported in the same brief.
The new report field is required in the JSON schema, so the fake agent, the test helpers and the literal in run_pin_tests.rs must emit it.

acceptance_criteria.text: ProducerOutput in crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs has a criteria_check field (criterion, status, evidence per entry). producer_schema() includes it and the existing schema test covers it.

crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md tells the producer to check its work against each accepted acceptance criterion and to report the result in criteria_check, and says that an unmet criterion is sent back once and then fails the job.

produce_and_verify in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs sends a report back to the producer when any accepted criterion is unmet or missing from criteria_check. The send-back brief names every such criterion, and the producer's UI line says so.

Run `cargo test --locked`. A new lifecycle test has the scripted producer first report one criterion unmet and then report all criteria met. It asserts that the producer runs twice before the first Verifier invocation, that the send-back brief text contains the unmet criterion, that the job lands, and that the verifier is never the first to see the unmet criterion.

Run `cargo test --locked`. A second new test has the producer still report a criterion unmet after the send-back. It asserts that the job ends Failed with a reason naming the criterion and that no Verifier invocation happened.

Run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`. All three pass, and the existing lifecycle tests still pass after the fake agent and test helpers were updated to emit criteria_check.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the pre-verification criteria check.

out_of_scope: Changing the verifier's own checking or its prompt.
Having Athena independently judge whether the producer's evidence for a criterion is true.
More than one send-back round, or changes to the test send-back budget.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or the CI workflows.
departures: The change touches the producer schema and every fixture that emits a producer report, so cost and time sit above the reference. Pass probability is slightly lower because there is design latitude in the self-check mechanism.
